socrates.name: Socrates
socrates.bio: Pursued truth through the method of dialectical questioning, held that "the unexamined life is not worth living," and was finally sentenced by Athens to die by drinking hemlock.

plato.name: Plato
plato.bio: A student of Socrates, he founded the Academy in Athens, proposed the Theory of Forms, and wrote the Republic.

aristotle.name: Aristotle
aristotle.bio: A student of Plato and the teacher of Alexander the Great, his works span logic, biology, politics and ethics.

alexander.name: Alexander the Great
alexander.bio: In ten years he built an empire stretching from Greece and Egypt to the Indus River, opening the Hellenistic age.

philip2.name: Philip II of Macedon
philip2.bio: Reformed the Macedonian army and conquered the Greek city-states, laying the foundation for his son Alexander's eastern campaigns.

darius3.name: Darius III
darius3.bio: The last emperor of the Achaemenid dynasty, he was defeated by Alexander at the Battle of Gaugamela.

caesar.name: Julius Caesar
caesar.bio: Conquered Gaul, crossed the Rubicon to launch a civil war, and was assassinated after becoming dictator for life.

pompey.name: Pompey
pompey.bio: Formed the First Triumvirate with Caesar and Crassus, later broke with Caesar, and after military defeat fled to Egypt, where he was killed.

crassus.name: Crassus
crassus.bio: Rome's richest man and a member of the First Triumvirate, he died after being defeated by Parthia at the Battle of Carrhae.

brutus.name: Brutus
brutus.bio: One of the chief conspirators in Caesar's assassination; Caesar is said to have uttered "You too, Brutus?" as he lay dying.

augustus.name: Augustus
augustus.role: First emperor of the Roman Empire
augustus.bio: Caesar's adopted son; after defeating Antony and Cleopatra he established the principate and began the Pax Romana.

antony.name: Mark Antony
antony.bio: A lieutenant of Caesar and member of the Second Triumvirate, he allied with Cleopatra and was defeated by Octavian at the Battle of Actium.

cleopatra.name: Cleopatra VII
cleopatra.bio: The last pharaoh of the Ptolemaic dynasty, she allied first with Caesar and then with Antony; with her death Egypt was annexed to Rome.

confucius.name: Confucius
confucius.bio: Founder of Confucianism, he advocated benevolence and ritual propriety and taught students regardless of background; his disciples compiled his words and deeds into the Analects.

laozi.name: Laozi
laozi.bio: Founder of Daoism, traditionally credited with writing the Tao Te Ching; according to the Records of the Grand Historian, Confucius once consulted him on ritual. (Birth and death years follow the traditional account.)

mencius.name: Mencius
mencius.bio: A student of Zisi's disciples, he developed Confucius's teachings, put forward the theory that human nature is good and the idea that the people are more important than the ruler, and is honored as the "Second Sage."

xunzi.name: Xunzi
xunzi.bio: A Confucian of the late Warring States period who argued that human nature is evil and valued ritual and law together; his students included Han Fei and Li Si.

hanfei.name: Han Fei
hanfei.bio: Synthesized Legalism by stressing law, technique and authority; he was greatly admired by King Zheng of Qin but was framed and killed by his fellow student Li Si.

lisi.name: Li Si
lisi.bio: Helped the First Emperor of Qin unify the six states, implemented the commandery-county system and a unified script, and was later framed by Zhao Gao and cut in two at the waist.

qinshihuang.name: Qin Shi Huang
qinshihuang.role: Founding emperor of the Qin dynasty
qinshihuang.bio: Unified China in 221 BC, styled himself the First Emperor, and standardized writing, weights and measures, and currency.

xiangyu.name: Xiang Yu
xiangyu.bio: A leader of the uprisings at the end of Qin, he crushed the Qin army at the Battle of Julu, lost to Liu Bang in the Chu–Han Contention, and killed himself at the Wu River.

liubang.name: Liu Bang
liubang.role: Founding emperor of the Han dynasty
liubang.bio: Born a commoner and skilled at employing talent, he defeated Xiang Yu and founded the Han dynasty.

hanxin.name: Han Xin
hanxin.role: Famed general of the early Han
hanxin.bio: "Without peer in the realm," he won half of Liu Bang's empire for him, and was later killed in a scheme by Empress Lü and Xiao He.

zhangliang.name: Zhang Liang
zhangliang.bio: "Devising strategies within the command tent to decide victory a thousand miles away"; after success he withdrew from public life at the height of his glory.

caocao.name: Cao Cao
caocao.bio: Controlled the emperor to command the warlords, unified the north, and laid the foundation of Cao Wei; he was also an outstanding poet.

liubei.name: Liu Bei
liubei.bio: Famed for his benevolence, he paid three visits to the thatched cottage to recruit Zhuge Liang and founded Shu Han.

sunquan.name: Sun Quan
sunquan.bio: Inherited the holdings of his father and elder brother in Jiangdong and, allied with Liu Bei, repulsed Cao Cao at Red Cliffs.

zhugeliang.name: Zhuge Liang
zhugeliang.bio: Proposed the Longzhong Plan and served Liu Bei and his son, devoting himself to the cause until his death.

guanyu.name: Guan Yu
guanyu.bio: Renowned for loyalty and righteousness, he was later venerated as Emperor Guansheng; he was killed by Eastern Wu after the loss of Jing Province.

zhouyu.name: Zhou Yu
zhouyu.bio: Commander of the Wu forces at the Battle of Red Cliffs, he crushed Cao Cao's army with a fire attack.

simayi.name: Sima Yi
simayi.bio: Repeatedly fended off Zhuge Liang's Northern Expeditions; his grandson Sima Yan usurped Wei and founded the Jin dynasty.

lorenzo.name: Lorenzo de' Medici
lorenzo.bio: Known as "Lorenzo the Magnificent," he generously patronized artists and made Florence the center of the Renaissance.

verrocchio.name: Andrea del Verrocchio
verrocchio.bio: Owner of a leading workshop in Florence, where Leonardo da Vinci served as an apprentice.

davinci.name: Leonardo da Vinci
davinci.bio: Author of the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper; his manuscripts cover anatomy, engineering and ideas for flying machines.

michelangelo.name: Michelangelo
michelangelo.bio: Created the statue of David and the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel; in his youth he lived in the Medici household.

raphael.name: Raphael
raphael.bio: Author of The School of Athens, in which he painted Plato with the features of Leonardo da Vinci.

machiavelli.name: Niccolò Machiavelli
machiavelli.bio: Wrote The Prince and dedicated the book to Lorenzo II de' Medici.

julius2.name: Pope Julius II
julius2.bio: The "Warrior Pope," he commissioned Michelangelo to paint the Sistine ceiling and Raphael to paint the frescoes of the Vatican rooms.

nobunaga.name: Oda Nobunaga
nobunaga.bio: Pursued unification through firearm tactics and the free-market policy of rakuichi-rakuza, and was killed by Akechi Mitsuhide in the Honnō-ji Incident.

hideyoshi.name: Toyotomi Hideyoshi
hideyoshi.bio: Born a peasant, he completed the unification of Japan after Nobunaga's death and in his later years sent armies to Korea.

ieyasu.name: Tokugawa Ieyasu
ieyasu.role: First shogun of the Edo shogunate
ieyasu.bio: After his victory at Sekigahara he founded the Edo shogunate, which lasted about 260 years.

mitsuhide.name: Akechi Mitsuhide
mitsuhide.bio: A senior retainer of the Oda clan, he launched the Honnō-ji Incident and was soon defeated by Hideyoshi at the Battle of Yamazaki.

yisunsin.name: Yi Sun-sin
yisunsin.bio: During the Imjin War he repeatedly defeated the Japanese navy with turtle ships, and was killed at the Battle of Noryang.

shingen.name: Takeda Shingen
shingen.bio: The "Tiger of Kai," he inflicted a major defeat on Tokugawa Ieyasu at the Battle of Mikatagahara.

kenshin.name: Uesugi Kenshin
kenshin.bio: The "Dragon of Echigo," he fought Takeda Shingen many times at Kawanakajima.

copernicus.name: Nicolaus Copernicus
copernicus.bio: Proposed the heliocentric theory and wrote On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres, setting off the Scientific Revolution.

galileo.name: Galileo Galilei
galileo.bio: Improved the telescope and observed the moons of Jupiter; he was tried by the Inquisition for supporting heliocentrism.

kepler.name: Johannes Kepler
kepler.bio: Using Tycho's observational data, he formulated the three laws of planetary motion.

tycho.name: Tycho Brahe
tycho.bio: A Danish astronomer who left the most accurate astronomical observations made before the invention of the telescope.

newton.name: Isaac Newton
newton.bio: Proposed universal gravitation and the three laws of motion and developed calculus, "standing on the shoulders of giants."

leibniz.name: Gottfried Leibniz
leibniz.bio: Invented calculus independently of Newton, giving rise to a bitter priority dispute.

darwin.name: Charles Darwin
darwin.bio: Voyaged around the world aboard the Beagle and wrote On the Origin of Species, proposing the theory of evolution by natural selection.

einstein.name: Albert Einstein
einstein.bio: Proposed relativity and the light-quantum hypothesis, and won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921.

washington.name: George Washington
washington.role: First president of the United States
washington.bio: Led the Continental Army to victory in the War of Independence and voluntarily stepped down after two terms as president.

lafayette.name: Marquis de Lafayette
lafayette.bio: Volunteered for the American War of Independence and became as close as a son to Washington; he later took part in drafting the Declaration of the Rights of Man.

jefferson.name: Thomas Jefferson
jefferson.role: Third president of the United States
jefferson.bio: Principal author of the Declaration of Independence; during his presidency he completed the Louisiana Purchase.

louis16.name: Louis XVI
louis16.bio: His support for the American War of Independence worsened France's finances, and he was sent to the guillotine during the French Revolution.

marie.name: Marie Antoinette
marie.bio: An Austrian archduchess and wife of Louis XVI, she was executed during the Revolution.

robespierre.name: Maximilien Robespierre
robespierre.bio: A central figure of the Reign of Terror, he was executed after the Thermidorian coup.

napoleon.name: Napoleon Bonaparte
napoleon.bio: A military genius who rose after the Revolution, he promulgated the Napoleonic Code and was finally defeated at Waterloo.

wellington.name: Duke of Wellington
wellington.bio: Defeated Napoleon at the Battle of Waterloo together with the Prussian allied forces.

alexander1.name: Alexander I of Russia
alexander1.bio: Repulsed Napoleon's invasion in 1812 and led the Holy Alliance after the Congress of Vienna.

beethoven.name: Ludwig van Beethoven
beethoven.bio: He originally dedicated the Eroica Symphony to Napoleon, but angrily scratched out the dedication on learning that Napoleon had crowned himself emperor.

sunyatsen.name: Sun Yat-sen
sunyatsen.role: Founding father of the Republic of China
sunyatsen.bio: Led the revolution that overthrew the Qing dynasty, proposed the Three Principles of the People, and founded the Kuomintang of China.

chiangkaishek.name: Chiang Kai-shek
chiangkaishek.role: President of the Republic of China
chiangkaishek.bio: Unified the country through the Northern Expedition and led the war of resistance against Japan; after losing the Chinese Civil War his government moved to Taiwan.

maozedong.name: Mao Zedong
maozedong.role: Chairman of the People's Republic of China
maozedong.bio: Leader of the Chinese Communist Party, he founded the People's Republic of China in 1949 and launched the Great Leap Forward and the Cultural Revolution.

churchill.name: Winston Churchill
churchill.bio: Led Britain in resisting Nazi Germany in World War II and won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1953.

fdr.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
fdr.bio: Carried out the New Deal to combat the Great Depression and led the United States into World War II; the only president elected to four terms.

stalin.name: Joseph Stalin
stalin.bio: Pushed industrialization and collectivization, carried out the Great Purge, and led the Soviet Union to defeat Nazi Germany.

hitler.name: Adolf Hitler
hitler.bio: Launched World War II and the Holocaust, and committed suicide before defeat.

gandhi.name: Mahatma Gandhi
gandhi.role: Leader of the Indian independence movement
gandhi.bio: Fought for Indian independence through nonviolent non-cooperation, influencing civil rights movements around the world.

mlk.name: Martin Luther King Jr.
mlk.bio: Inspired by Gandhi, he led the African American civil rights movement in the United States and delivered the "I Have a Dream" speech.

mandela.name: Nelson Mandela
mandela.bio: An anti-apartheid fighter who, after 27 years in prison, became South Africa's first Black president.

ptolemy1.name: Ptolemy I Soter
ptolemy1.bio: A general and biographer of Alexander; after Alexander's death he took possession of Egypt and founded the Museum and Library in Alexandria.

seleucus1.name: Seleucus I Nicator
seleucus1.bio: A general of Alexander who, after the Wars of the Diadochi, founded the Seleucid Empire stretching from Syria to the Iranian plateau.

hephaestion.name: Hephaestion
hephaestion.bio: Alexander the Great's closest friend since childhood and his deputy, rising to the rank of chiliarch; Alexander was inconsolable after Hephaestion died of illness.

euclid.name: Euclid
euclid.bio: Active in Alexandria in the time of Ptolemy I, his Elements was the most widely circulated mathematics textbook. (Birth and death years are estimates.)

archimedes.name: Archimedes
archimedes.bio: A native of Syracuse in Sicily, he discovered the principles of buoyancy and the lever, and was killed when the Roman army took Syracuse.

cyrus.name: Cyrus the Great
cyrus.bio: Founded the Achaemenid Persian Empire and was known for his lenient treatment of conquered peoples, allowing the Jews in Babylon to return home. (Birth year is an estimate.)

xenophon.name: Xenophon
xenophon.bio: A student of Socrates, he led Greek mercenaries back from the heart of Persia and wrote the Anabasis and the Cyropaedia.

demosthenes.name: Demosthenes
demosthenes.bio: Athens's greatest orator, he delivered the Philippics calling on the Greek city-states to resist Macedon, and in the end took poison to end his life.

cicero.name: Cicero
cicero.bio: Rome's most famous orator and prose writer, he defended the republican system and was killed after delivering the Philippics attacking Antony.

cato.name: Cato the Younger
cato.bio: A republican leader famed for his integrity and incorruptibility, he opposed Caesar all his life and killed himself after his defeat at Utica.

cassius.name: Gaius Cassius Longinus
cassius.bio: One of the chief conspirators in Caesar's assassination; at the Battle of Philippi he mistakenly believed all was lost and killed himself.

lepidus.name: Marcus Aemilius Lepidus
lepidus.bio: Caesar's master of the horse, he formed the Second Triumvirate with Octavian and Antony, and was later stripped of his military command by Octavian.

agrippa.name: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa
agrippa.bio: Octavian's closest friend and chief general, he commanded the victory at Actium and built the original Pantheon.

octavia.name: Octavia the Younger
octavia.bio: Octavian's elder sister, she married Antony to strengthen the alliance, and was later divorced by Antony for the sake of Cleopatra.

virgil.name: Virgil
virgil.bio: Rome's greatest poet, he wrote the epic Aeneid with the support of Augustus.

zhuangzi.name: Zhuangzi
zhuangzi.bio: A representative Daoist of the Warring States period, he expounded the way of free and easy wandering and the equality of all things through parables; together with Laozi he is known as "Lao-Zhuang."

mozi.name: Mozi
mozi.bio: Founder of Mohism, he advocated universal love, opposition to aggressive war, and thrift; in the Warring States period Mohism and Confucianism were together known as the two "prominent schools." (Birth and death years are estimates.)

shangyang.name: Shang Yang
shangyang.role: Reformer of the state of Qin
shangyang.bio: Assisted Duke Xiao of Qin in two rounds of reform, laying the foundation of Qin's wealth and power; after Duke Xiao's death he was executed by being torn apart by chariots.

zhaogao.name: Zhao Gao
zhaogao.bio: After the death of the First Emperor of Qin he conspired with Li Si to install Huhai, and left behind the story of "calling a deer a horse"; he was later killed by Ziying. (Birth year unknown.)

huhai.name: Qin Er Shi
huhai.role: Second emperor of the Qin dynasty
huhai.bio: The youngest son of the First Emperor of Qin, he seized the throne through the Shaqiu conspiracy, employed Zhao Gao and imposed excessive punishments, and was finally forced to commit suicide.

fusu.name: Fusu
fusu.role: Eldest prince of the Qin dynasty
fusu.bio: Eldest son of the First Emperor of Qin; for remonstrating against the burying of the scholars he was sent to the northern frontier as army supervisor, and was ordered to die by a forged edict. (Birth year unknown.)

mengtian.name: Meng Tian
mengtian.bio: Led an army of 300,000 north against the Xiongnu and built the Great Wall; like Fusu, he was forced to death by a forged edict. (Birth year unknown.)

xiaohe.name: Xiao He
xiaohe.bio: One of the "Three Heroes of the Early Han," he first secured Qin's laws and maps when entering Xianyang, and after "chasing Han Xin under the moon" later helped Empress Lü to put him to death.

lvhou.name: Empress Lü
lvhou.bio: Liu Bang's empress; after his death she ruled as regent, the first empress in Chinese history to hold real power.

zhangfei.name: Zhang Fei
zhangfei.bio: Like Guan Yu, one of Liu Bei's earliest followers, he held off pursuers at the Changban Bridge, and was later assassinated by his subordinates. (Birth year is an estimate.)

zhaoyun.name: Zhao Yun
zhaoyun.bio: At the Battle of Changban he protected the infant lord Liu Shan and Lady Gan to safety, and was known for loyalty, courage and caution. (Birth year unknown.)

lvbu.name: Lü Bu
lvbu.role: Warlord of the late Eastern Han
lvbu.bio: Brave and skilled in battle but fickle, he killed Ding Yuan and then Dong Zhuo, and was finally captured and killed by Cao Cao at Xiapi. (Birth year unknown.)

dongzhuo.name: Dong Zhuo
dongzhuo.role: Powerful minister of the Eastern Han
dongzhuo.bio: Led the Xiliang army into Luoyang, deposed the young emperor and installed Emperor Xian, ruled tyrannically and provoked the Guandong coalition to attack him, and was later killed by Lü Bu. (Birth year unknown.)

yuanshao.name: Yuan Shao
yuanshao.role: Warlord of the late Eastern Han
yuanshao.bio: Born into a family that had held the Three Excellencies for four generations, he was once leader of the coalition against Dong Zhuo, held Hebei, and lost to Cao Cao at the Battle of Guandu.

caopi.name: Cao Pi
caopi.bio: Son of Cao Cao, he accepted the abdication of Emperor Xian of Han and founded Cao Wei; he wrote the earliest treatise of literary criticism in China, "Discourse on Literature" in the Dianlun.

liushan.name: Liu Shan
liushan.bio: Son of Liu Bei, he reigned for forty-one years; after surrendering to Wei he left behind the saying "Happy here, I do not think of Shu."

sunce.name: Sun Ce
sunce.bio: The "Little Conqueror," he pacified Jiangdong with his father Sun Jian's old troops, and was assassinated at twenty-six, passing his legacy to his younger brother Sun Quan.

lusu.name: Lu Su
lusu.bio: Strongly advocated a Sun–Liu alliance against Cao Cao, took over military command after Zhou Yu's death, and once went to a meeting with Guan Yu armed only with a single sword.

lvmeng.name: Lü Meng
lvmeng.bio: He applied himself to study, giving rise to the saying "After three days apart, look at a scholar with new eyes," and crossed the river in disguise to capture Jing Province.

luxun.name: Lu Xun
luxun.bio: At the Battle of Yiling he decisively defeated Liu Bei by burning his linked camps, and later rose to the post of chancellor of Eastern Wu.

xiandi.name: Emperor Xian of Han
xiandi.role: Last emperor of the Eastern Han
xiandi.bio: Installed by Dong Zhuo and later taken to Xu by Cao Cao, he finally abdicated in favor of Cao Pi, ending the Eastern Han.

sunjian.name: Sun Jian
sunjian.role: General of the late Eastern Han
sunjian.bio: Father of Sun Ce and Sun Quan, he was the first to enter Luoyang in the campaign against Dong Zhuo, and was killed in an ambush while campaigning against Liu Biao.

dante.name: Dante Alighieri
dante.bio: Wrote the Divine Comedy in the Tuscan dialect and is hailed as the "Father of the Italian language," heralding the Renaissance.

cosimo.name: Cosimo de' Medici
cosimo.role: Banker and de facto ruler of Florence
cosimo.bio: Founder of the Medici family's power, he patronized Brunelleschi, Donatello and others, and supported the Platonic Academy.

perugino.name: Pietro Perugino
perugino.bio: Trained in the workshop of Verrocchio, he took part in painting the walls of the Sistine Chapel and was the teacher of Raphael.

savonarola.name: Girolamo Savonarola
savonarola.bio: Gained control of Florence through apocalyptic sermons and launched the "Bonfire of the Vanities"; he was finally burned at the stake by the papacy.

alexander6.name: Pope Alexander VI
alexander6.bio: From the Spanish Borgia family, he was known for nepotism and scheming, and drew the line dividing Spain's and Portugal's overseas territories.

cesareborgia.name: Cesare Borgia
cesareborgia.bio: Son of Pope Alexander VI, he built a power base in Romagna through force and cunning, and was regarded by Machiavelli as a model of the new prince.

ludovico.name: Ludovico Sforza
ludovico.bio: Known as "il Moro," he invited Leonardo da Vinci to the Milanese court and was later captured by French forces and died in prison.

leo10.name: Pope Leo X
leo10.bio: Son of Lorenzo the Magnificent, he was a lavish patron of the arts and sold indulgences to fund the rebuilding of St. Peter's Basilica, setting off the Reformation.

francis1.name: Francis I of France
francis1.bio: Brought the Renaissance to France, supported Leonardo da Vinci in his later years, and long contested Italy with Charles V.

erasmus.name: Erasmus
erasmus.bio: A leading figure of the Northern Renaissance, he edited the Greek New Testament and wrote In Praise of Folly.

luther.name: Martin Luther
luther.bio: In 1517 he posted the Ninety-five Theses against indulgences, beginning the Reformation, and translated the Bible into German.

charles5.name: Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor
charles5.role: Holy Roman Emperor and King of Spain
charles5.bio: Ruled the "empire on which the sun never sets," stretching from Spain and the Netherlands to the Americas, and confronted Luther at the Diet of Worms.

oichi.name: Oichi
oichi.bio: The foremost beauty of the Sengoku period, she married first Azai Nagamasa and then Shibata Katsuie, and finally died by suicide together with Katsuie.

asai.name: Azai Nagamasa
asai.bio: Married Nobunaga's sister Oichi, later broke the alliance and joined the anti-Nobunaga camp, and killed himself when Odani Castle fell.

shibata.name: Shibata Katsuie
shibata.role: Senior retainer of the Oda clan
shibata.bio: Chief elder of the Oda clan, known as "Oni Shibata" (Demon Shibata); after Nobunaga's death he was defeated by Hideyoshi at the Battle of Shizugatake.

yoshiaki.name: Ashikaga Yoshiaki
yoshiaki.role: Last shogun of the Muromachi shogunate
yoshiaki.bio: Installed as shogun when Nobunaga escorted him into Kyoto, he later plotted the "Nobunaga encirclement" and was exiled in return, ending the Muromachi shogunate.

ishida.name: Ishida Mitsunari
ishida.bio: One of the Five Commissioners of the Toyotomi regime, after Hideyoshi's death he rallied the Western Army against Tokugawa Ieyasu, and was beheaded after losing at Sekigahara.

konishi.name: Konishi Yukinaga
konishi.bio: A Christian daimyo who led the Japanese vanguard in the Imjin War; after Sekigahara he was executed together with Ishida Mitsunari.

sanada.name: Sanada Yukimura
sanada.bio: Real name Sanada Nobushige, at the Summer Siege of Osaka he charged Ieyasu's headquarters with his red-armored cavalry and was acclaimed "Japan's foremost warrior."

hideyori.name: Toyotomi Hideyori
hideyori.bio: The heir born to Hideyoshi in his later years; after the Siege of Osaka he killed himself with his mother Yodo-dono in Osaka Castle, and the Toyotomi clan perished.

yodo.name: Yodo-dono
yodo.bio: Eldest daughter of Azai Nagamasa and Oichi, concubine of Hideyoshi and mother of Hideyori, she effectively directed the Toyotomi house in Osaka Castle.

descartes.name: René Descartes
descartes.bio: Proposed "I think, therefore I am" and founded analytic geometry; known as the father of modern philosophy.

humboldt.name: Alexander von Humboldt
humboldt.bio: Explored the Americas for five years and founded physical geography, influencing a whole generation including Darwin and Bolívar.

planck.name: Max Planck
planck.bio: In 1900 he proposed the hypothesis of energy quantization, founding quantum theory, and won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1918.

bohr.name: Niels Bohr
bohr.bio: Proposed the quantum model of the atom and founded the Copenhagen school; won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1922.

heisenberg.name: Werner Heisenberg
heisenberg.bio: Proposed matrix mechanics and the uncertainty principle, and led German nuclear fission research during World War II.

oppenheimer.name: J. Robert Oppenheimer
oppenheimer.bio: Director of the Los Alamos Laboratory of the Manhattan Project, known as the "father of the atomic bomb"; after the war he opposed developing the hydrogen bomb.

franklin.name: Benjamin Franklin
franklin.bio: Studied lightning with his kite experiment, took part in drafting the Declaration of Independence, and as envoy to France won crucial aid.

johnadams.name: John Adams
johnadams.role: Second president of the United States
johnadams.bio: A leader of the independence movement and Washington's vice president, he went from comrade to political rival of Jefferson; they reconciled in old age and died on the same day.

hamilton.name: Alexander Hamilton
hamilton.role: First U.S. Secretary of the Treasury
hamilton.bio: Washington's aide-de-camp and principal author of the Federalist Papers, he built the American financial system and died in a duel with Burr.

madison.name: James Madison
madison.role: Fourth president of the United States
madison.bio: The "Father of the Constitution," he drafted the Bill of Rights, and the War of 1812 between the United States and Britain broke out during his presidency.

paine.name: Thomas Paine
paine.bio: His pamphlet Common Sense ignited public opinion for American independence; he later went to France to take part in the Revolution and wrote The Rights of Man.

george3.name: George III
george3.bio: He lost the Thirteen Colonies of North America during his reign and also led Britain against Napoleon; he went insane in his old age.

talleyrand.name: Charles Maurice de Talleyrand-Périgord
talleyrand.bio: A diplomat who stood firm through the Revolution, Napoleon and the Bourbon Restoration, he won concessions for defeated France at the Congress of Vienna.

metternich.name: Klemens von Metternich
metternich.bio: Directed the Congress of Vienna and established the "Metternich system" that maintained the European balance of power; he fell from power in the Revolutions of 1848.

marx.name: Karl Marx
marx.bio: Co-wrote the Communist Manifesto with Engels and wrote Das Kapital; his doctrines profoundly influenced twentieth-century politics.

lenin.name: Vladimir Lenin
lenin.bio: Led the Bolsheviks in the October Revolution and established the world's first socialist state.

songqingling.name: Soong Ching-ling
songqingling.bio: Wife of Sun Yat-sen and one of the Soong sisters; after 1949 she served as vice chairwoman of the People's Republic of China.

songmeiling.name: Soong Mei-ling
songmeiling.bio: Wife of Chiang Kai-shek; during the war of resistance she addressed the U.S. Congress to win aid, and was known as the "First Lady."

wangjingwei.name: Wang Jingwei
wangjingwei.bio: In his early years he gained fame by attempting to assassinate the Prince Regent, and transcribed Sun Yat-sen's will; during the war of resistance he defected to Japan and set up the Nanjing National Government.

farabi.name: Al-Farabi
farabi.bio: Famed for his commentaries on Aristotle, he is honored as the "Second Teacher," and conceived an ideal city based on Plato.

avicenna.name: Avicenna
avicenna.bio: Latinized as Avicenna, his Canon of Medicine was used as a medical textbook in Europe for hundreds of years.

averroes.name: Averroes
averroes.bio: Latinized as Averroes, born in Córdoba, he profoundly influenced medieval Europe through his systematic commentaries on Aristotle's works.

maimonides.name: Maimonides
maimonides.bio: Born in Córdoba, he later served as court physician to the Ayyubid dynasty in Cairo and wrote the Guide for the Perplexed.

genghis.name: Genghis Khan
genghis.role: First great khan of the Mongol Empire
genghis.bio: Born Temüjin, he unified the Mongol tribes and then campaigned west against Khwarazm, laying the foundations of the largest contiguous land empire in human history.

borte.name: Börte
borte.bio: Principal wife of Genghis Khan, she bore four sons, Jochi, Chagatai, Ögedei and Tolui, and held great prestige among the people.

jochi.name: Jochi
jochi.bio: Eldest son of Genghis Khan, he was estranged from his brothers by doubts over his parentage; his domain later developed into the Golden Horde.

ogedei.name: Ögedei Khan
ogedei.role: Second great khan of the Mongol Empire
ogedei.bio: Third son of Genghis Khan, he destroyed the Jin dynasty, launched the Western Campaign of the eldest princes, and established the capital at Karakorum.

tolui.name: Tolui
tolui.bio: Youngest son of Genghis Khan, he inherited his father's main army; his sons Möngke, Kublai and Hulagu each became rulers of a domain.

sorghaghtani.name: Sorghaghtani Beki
sorghaghtani.bio: A princess of the Keraite tribe who, after being widowed, schemed so that her four sons produced two great khans and one Ilkhan.

mongke.name: Möngke Khan
mongke.role: Fourth great khan of the Mongol Empire
mongke.bio: Eldest son of Tolui, he sent Hulagu on the Western Campaign and Kublai to administer the Han lands; while leading the campaign against Southern Song he died at Diaoyu Fortress.

kublai.name: Kublai Khan
kublai.bio: Founded the Yuan dynasty and destroyed Southern Song, made Dadu his capital, and failed in both of his invasions of Japan.

hulagu.name: Hulagu Khan
hulagu.bio: In 1258 he captured Baghdad, ending the Abbasid dynasty; his army was defeated by the Mamluks at Ain Jalut.

batu.name: Batu Khan
batu.bio: Son of Jochi, he commanded the Western Campaign of the eldest princes, sweeping across the Rus' principalities and penetrating deep into Poland and Hungary.

subutai.name: Subutai
subutai.bio: One of Genghis Khan's "Four Hounds," he commanded dozens of campaigns in his lifetime, ranging from China to Eastern Europe.

xuanzong.name: Emperor Xuanzong of Tang
xuanzong.bio: Created the prosperous Kaiyuan era; in old age he doted on Yang Guifei and tired of government, and after the An Lushan Rebellion fled in haste to Shu.

yangguifei.name: Yang Guifei
yangguifei.role: Consort of Emperor Xuanzong of Tang
yangguifei.bio: One of the Four Great Beauties of ancient China, she was ordered to die at Mawei Post Station during the An Lushan Rebellion.

anlushan.name: An Lushan
anlushan.bio: Military governor of three circuits, he rose in revolt against the Tang in 755, setting off the An Lushan Rebellion, and was later killed by his son.

libai.name: Li Bai
libai.bio: The "Immortal of Poetry," his style was bold and unfettered; he once served as a Hanlin attendant and in old age was exiled to Yelang for being drawn into the rebellion of Prince Yong.

dufu.name: Du Fu
dufu.bio: The "Sage of Poetry," he recorded in verse the hardships of ordinary people before and after the An Lushan Rebellion and is called the "poet-historian."

baijuyi.name: Bai Juyi
baijuyi.bio: Promoted the New Yuefu movement; his "Song of Everlasting Sorrow" and "Song of the Pipa" spread throughout East Asia and were greatly esteemed in Japan's Heian court.

hanyu.name: Han Yu
hanyu.bio: Foremost of the Eight Great Prose Masters of the Tang and Song, he advocated the Classical Prose Movement and was demoted to Chaozhou for his "Memorial on the Buddha's Bone."

ouyangxiu.name: Ouyang Xiu
ouyangxiu.bio: A leader of the Northern Song literary world, he presided over the civil service examinations that promoted Su Shi, Su Zhe, Zeng Gong and others, and compiled the New Book of Tang and the New History of the Five Dynasties.

wanganshi.name: Wang Anshi
wanganshi.role: Chancellor and reformer of the Northern Song
wanganshi.bio: Led the Xining reforms, implementing the Green Sprouts Law, the Baojia system and others, which triggered factional struggles between the old and new parties.

simaguang.name: Sima Guang
simaguang.bio: Leader of the conservative faction, he edited the annalistic general history Zizhi Tongjian, and in old age became chancellor and abolished all the new laws.

sushi.name: Su Shi
sushi.bio: Styled Dongpo Jushi, he excelled in poetry, ci, prose, calligraphy and painting; demoted to Huangzhou after the Crow Terrace Poetry Case, he wrote the "Ode to Red Cliff."

suzhe.name: Su Zhe
suzhe.bio: Younger brother of Su Shi; with his father and elder brother he is known as the "Three Sus," and is likewise one of the Eight Great Prose Masters of the Tang and Song.

zhuxi.name: Zhu Xi
zhuxi.bio: Synthesizer of Song Neo-Confucianism, his Collected Commentaries on the Four Books became the standard textbook for the civil service examinations in the Yuan, Ming and Qing.

zhuyuanzhang.name: Hongwu Emperor
zhuyuanzhang.role: Founding emperor of the Ming dynasty
zhuyuanzhang.bio: Born to a poor peasant family and once a monk, he overthrew the Yuan dynasty and founded the Ming, abolishing the chancellor's office and strengthening imperial power.

wanli.name: Wanli Emperor
wanli.bio: Reigning forty-eight years, he saw the Zhang Juzheng reforms early on but neglected government for long periods later, and sent troops to aid Korea against Japan.

matteoricci.name: Matteo Ricci
matteoricci.bio: An Italian missionary who drew the "Complete Map of the Myriad Countries of the World" and was permitted to settle in Beijing, opening scholarly exchange between China and the West.

xuguangqi.name: Xu Guangqi
xuguangqi.bio: Co-translated the Elements with Matteo Ricci, compiled the Complete Treatise on Agriculture, and directed the revision of the Chongzhen Calendar.

kangxi.name: Kangxi Emperor
kangxi.bio: Reigning sixty-one years, he suppressed the Revolt of the Three Feudatories, recovered Taiwan, and signed the Treaty of Nerchinsk with Russia.

hongxiuquan.name: Hong Xiuquan
hongxiuquan.role: Heavenly King of the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom
hongxiuquan.bio: After repeatedly failing the examinations he claimed to be the son of God, founded the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom with its capital at Tianjing, and fought the Qing court for more than ten years.

zengguofan.name: Zeng Guofan
zengguofan.bio: Raised the Xiang Army to suppress the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom and promoted the Self-Strengthening Movement; regarded as a leading statesman of the late Qing "restoration."

lihongzhang.name: Li Hongzhang
lihongzhang.role: Senior statesman of the late Qing
lihongzhang.bio: Founder of the Huai Army and leader of the Self-Strengthening Movement, he signed the Treaty of Shimonoseki and the Boxer Protocol on behalf of the Qing court.

cixi.name: Empress Dowager Cixi
cixi.role: Empress dowager of the Qing dynasty
cixi.bio: Ruling from behind the curtain for nearly half a century, she launched the coup of 1898, imprisoning the Guangxu Emperor, and dominated late Qing politics.

guangxu.name: Guangxu Emperor
guangxu.bio: Supported the Hundred Days' Reform, was imprisoned on Yingtai after the coup, and died the day before Cixi's death.

kangyouwei.name: Kang Youwei
kangyouwei.bio: Initiated the Gongche Shangshu petition and led the Hundred Days' Reform; after its failure he went into exile abroad and organized the Baohuanghui (Protect the Emperor Society).

liangqichao.name: Liang Qichao
liangqichao.bio: A disciple of Kang Youwei, he enlightened a generation with essays in the "New Citizen style," and after the founding of the Republic opposed Yuan Shikai's attempt to become emperor.

yuanshikai.name: Yuan Shikai
yuanshikai.role: Beiyang leader and President of the Republic of China
yuanshikai.bio: Founder of the Beiyang New Army, he forced the Qing emperor to abdicate and became president; after eighty-three days as emperor he died amid opposition.

puyi.name: Puyi
puyi.role: Last emperor of the Qing dynasty
puyi.bio: Enthroned at three and abdicating at six, he later became emperor of Japan-sponsored Manchukuo, and in his last years worked as a gardener at the botanical garden in Beijing.

henry7.name: Henry VII of England
henry7.bio: Defeated Richard III at the Battle of Bosworth Field, ended the Wars of the Roses and founded the Tudor dynasty.

henry8.name: Henry VIII
henry8.bio: Broke with the papacy over his divorce and made himself Supreme Head of the Church of England; he married six times in his life.

catherineofaragon.name: Catherine of Aragon
catherineofaragon.bio: A Spanish princess and the first queen of Henry VIII, she was set aside for failing to bear a male heir; mother of Mary I.

anneboleyn.name: Anne Boleyn
anneboleyn.bio: Second queen of Henry VIII and mother of Elizabeth I, she was beheaded on charges of adultery and treason.

wolsey.name: Thomas Wolsey
wolsey.bio: Henry VIII's most trusted minister in his early reign, he fell from power after failing to secure the divorce and died while being taken under escort.

thomasmore.name: Thomas More
thomasmore.bio: Author of Utopia, he was beheaded for refusing to recognize Henry VIII as head of the Church.

thomascromwell.name: Thomas Cromwell
thomascromwell.bio: Directed the English Reformation and the dissolution of the monasteries, and was executed after falling from favor over the failed Cleves marriage.

cranmer.name: Thomas Cranmer
cranmer.bio: Declared Henry VIII's first marriage invalid and compiled the Book of Common Prayer; he was burned at the stake under Mary I.

mary1.name: Mary I of England
mary1.bio: Restored Catholicism and persecuted Protestants, earning the name "Bloody Mary"; she married Philip II of Spain.

elizabeth1.name: Elizabeth I
elizabeth1.bio: The "Virgin Queen," she defeated the Spanish Armada, and English letters flourished during her reign.

maryqueenofscots.name: Mary, Queen of Scots
maryqueenofscots.bio: Forced to abdicate, she fled to England and was held in captivity for nineteen years; she was executed for involvement in a plot to assassinate Elizabeth.

philip2es.name: Philip II of Spain
philip2es.bio: Son of Charles V and husband of Mary I, he sent the Armada against England in 1588 and failed.

cecil.name: William Cecil, 1st Baron Burghley
cecil.bio: The minister Elizabeth I relied on most during her forty-year reign, later created Baron Burghley.

dudley.name: Robert Dudley, 1st Earl of Leicester
dudley.bio: Elizabeth I's childhood friend and favorite, once regarded as a possible royal husband.

walsingham.name: Francis Walsingham
walsingham.bio: Elizabeth's "spymaster," he uncovered the Babington Plot, which led to the execution of Mary, Queen of Scots.

drake.name: Francis Drake
drake.bio: Completed the first English circumnavigation of the globe and played a key role in repelling the Spanish Armada.

shakespeare.name: William Shakespeare
shakespeare.bio: The greatest writer in English literature, author of more than thirty plays including Hamlet and Romeo and Juliet.

james1.name: James VI and I
james1.bio: Son of Mary, Queen of Scots, he succeeded Elizabeth on the English throne and ordered the compilation of the King James Bible.

francisbacon.name: Francis Bacon
francisbacon.bio: Advocated the inductive method and experimental science, famous for the maxim "knowledge is power," and rose to be Lord Chancellor under James I.

spinoza.name: Baruch Spinoza
spinoza.bio: A Dutch philosopher of Jewish descent, expelled by the Jewish community; he wrote the Ethics, arguing that God is nature.

locke.name: John Locke
locke.bio: A leading empiricist whose Two Treatises of Government argued for the natural rights of life, liberty and property, influencing the founding of the United States.

montesquieu.name: Montesquieu
montesquieu.bio: Wrote The Spirit of the Laws, proposing the separation of powers into legislative, executive and judicial branches.

voltaire.name: Voltaire
voltaire.bio: A standard-bearer of the Enlightenment, he attacked the Church and absolutism with satire; author of Candide.

hume.name: David Hume
hume.bio: A representative of the Scottish Enlightenment whose skepticism about causation and induction profoundly influenced later philosophy.

rousseau.name: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
rousseau.bio: Wrote The Social Contract and Emile, advocating popular sovereignty, and became the spiritual banner of the French Revolution.

diderot.name: Denis Diderot
diderot.bio: Spent more than twenty years as chief editor of the Encyclopédie, gathering the knowledge and ideas of the Enlightenment.

frederick2.name: Frederick the Great
frederick2.bio: An enlightened despot, he seized Silesia and raised Prussia to a great power; he loved philosophy and the flute.

mariatheresa.name: Maria Theresa
mariatheresa.bio: The only female ruler of the Habsburg dynasty, she promoted reforms and had sixteen children.

adamsmith.name: Adam Smith
adamsmith.bio: Wrote The Wealth of Nations, setting out the division of labor and the "invisible hand"; hailed as the father of modern economics.

kant.name: Immanuel Kant
kant.bio: Wrote the Critique of Pure Reason, reconciling rationalism and empiricism, and defined enlightenment as "daring to know."

catherine2.name: Catherine the Great
catherine2.bio: A Russian empress of German birth, she corresponded with Enlightenment philosophers and expanded her territory to the Black Sea and Poland.

tagore.name: Rabindranath Tagore
tagore.bio: In 1913 he became the first Asian to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, and founded Visva-Bharati University.

jinnah.name: Muhammad Ali Jinnah
jinnah.bio: Leader of the Muslim League, he advocated the "two-nation theory" and pushed for the founding of Pakistan.

patel.name: Vallabhbhai Patel
patel.bio: The "Iron Man of India," he persuaded more than five hundred princely states to join India after independence.

nehru.name: Jawaharlal Nehru
nehru.bio: Gandhi's successor, he led India for seventeen years and promoted the Non-Aligned Movement.

ambedkar.name: B. R. Ambedkar
ambedkar.role: Chief drafter of the Indian Constitution
ambedkar.bio: Born into the untouchable caste, he fought for caste equality, presided over the drafting of the Indian Constitution, and in his last years led hundreds of thousands in converting to Buddhism.

bose.name: Subhas Chandra Bose
bose.role: Leader of the Indian independence movement
bose.bio: Advocated armed resistance against Britain, sought German and Japanese support in World War II to form the Indian National Army, and died in a plane crash in 1945.

mountbatten.name: Louis Mountbatten, 1st Earl Mountbatten of Burma
mountbatten.englishName: Louis Mountbatten, 1st Earl Mountbatten of Burma
mountbatten.role: British admiral and last Viceroy of India
mountbatten.bio: Supreme Allied Commander of the South East Asia Command in World War II, he oversaw the partition of India and Pakistan and the transfer of power in 1947.

indira.name: Indira Gandhi
indira.bio: Daughter of Nehru and India's first woman prime minister, she supported Bangladeshi independence in 1971 and was assassinated.

miranda.name: Francisco de Miranda
miranda.bio: A forerunner of Latin American independence, he took part in the American War of Independence and the French Revolution, and died in a Spanish prison.

toussaint.name: Toussaint Louverture
toussaint.bio: Led the Haitian slave revolution; after being lured into capture by Napoleon he died in a French prison, and Haiti became independent soon after.

bolivar.name: Simón Bolívar
bolivar.bio: Led Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia to independence from Spain, and is known as "El Libertador."

ferdinand7.name: Ferdinand VII
ferdinand7.bio: Forced to abdicate by Napoleon and held under house arrest in France, after his restoration he reinstated absolutism and tried to suppress the American independence movements.

mussolini.name: Benito Mussolini
mussolini.bio: Founded Fascism and ruled Italy as dictator for twenty years, allied with Germany and entered the war, and was executed by partisans upon defeat.

hirohito.name: Hirohito
hirohito.bio: Reigning sixty-two years through the invasion of China, the Pacific War and postwar reconstruction, he announced surrender in 1945 through the "Jewel Voice Broadcast."

tojo.name: Hideki Tojo
tojo.bio: Prime minister and army minister at the outbreak of the Pacific War, he was sentenced to death by hanging by the Tokyo Trials after the war.

goering.name: Hermann Göring
goering.role: Commander-in-chief of the German Air Force (Luftwaffe)
goering.bio: Number two in the Nazi regime, he directed the Battle of Britain and took poison before the Nuremberg Trials could execute him.

rommel.name: Erwin Rommel
rommel.bio: The "Desert Fox," he repeatedly defeated British forces in North Africa, later oversaw the defense of the Normandy coast, and was forced to kill himself over involvement in the plot to assassinate Hitler.

montgomery.name: Bernard Montgomery
montgomery.bio: Defeated Rommel at the Battle of El Alamein, turning the tide in North Africa, and later commanded the ground forces of the Normandy landings.

zhukov.name: Georgy Zhukov
zhukov.bio: Commanded the defense of Moscow, the counteroffensive at Stalingrad and the capture of Berlin; the Soviet Union's most outstanding general of World War II.

eisenhower.name: Dwight D. Eisenhower
eisenhower.role: Supreme Allied Commander and U.S. president
eisenhower.bio: Commanded the Normandy landings, became the first Supreme Allied Commander of NATO after the war, and served as U.S. president from 1953.

patton.name: George S. Patton
patton.bio: A renowned armored-warfare commander known for his dashing style, he led the Third Army sweeping across France and into Germany.

macarthur.name: Douglas MacArthur
macarthur.bio: Supreme Commander of Allied forces in the Pacific theater, he oversaw the Allied occupation of Japan after the war and was dismissed during the Korean War for advocating its expansion.

degaulle.name: Charles de Gaulle
degaulle.role: Leader of Free France and president of France
degaulle.bio: After the fall of France he called for resistance from London, and after the war founded the Fifth Republic and served as president.

truman.name: Harry S. Truman
truman.bio: Succeeded Roosevelt as president, ordered the dropping of the atomic bombs, and with the Truman Doctrine and Marshall Plan opened the Cold War.

kimilsung.name: Kim Il Sung
kimilsung.bio: Established the Democratic People's Republic of Korea with Soviet backing and launched the Korean War in 1950.

hochiminh.name: Ho Chi Minh
hochiminh.bio: Declared Vietnamese independence in 1945 and led the wars against France and the United States; honored as the father of the Vietnamese nation.

zhouenlai.name: Zhou Enlai
zhouenlai.role: Premier of the People's Republic of China
zhouenlai.bio: Premier for twenty-six years, he directed diplomacy including the Bandung Conference and the Sino-American rapprochement.

deng.name: Deng Xiaoping
deng.role: Leader of the Chinese Communist Party
deng.bio: Returned to power after the Cultural Revolution to push reform and opening-up, and ordered the June Fourth crackdown of 1989.

chiangchingkuo.name: Chiang Ching-kuo
chiangchingkuo.role: President of the Republic of China
chiangchingkuo.bio: Eldest son of Chiang Kai-shek, he promoted the Ten Major Construction Projects and in his last years lifted martial law, ended the ban on political parties and opened mainland family visits.

khrushchev.name: Nikita Khrushchev
khrushchev.bio: Delivered the Secret Speech criticizing Stalin, confronted Kennedy in the Cuban Missile Crisis, and was ousted in 1964.

brezhnev.name: Leonid Brezhnev
brezhnev.bio: In power for eighteen years, he pursued détente with the United States early on, then fell into stagnation and sent troops into Afghanistan.

kennedy.name: John F. Kennedy
kennedy.bio: Resolved the Cuban Missile Crisis and promoted the Moon landing program; he was assassinated in Dallas in 1963.

nixon.name: Richard Nixon
nixon.bio: Visited China in 1972, opening up U.S.–China relations, and because of Watergate became the only U.S. president to resign.

kissinger.name: Henry Kissinger
kissinger.bio: Nixon's national security adviser and secretary of state, he made a secret visit to China that helped normalize Sino-American relations.

castro.name: Fidel Castro
castro.bio: Overthrew the Batista regime in 1959 and ruled Cuba for nearly half a century.

cheguevara.name: Che Guevara
cheguevara.bio: An Argentine-born doctor who helped Castro win the Cuban Revolution; he was captured and executed while waging guerrilla warfare in Bolivia.

reagan.name: Ronald Reagan
reagan.bio: Confronted the Soviet Union with a hard line, called out "Tear down this wall," and signed the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty with Gorbachev.

thatcher.name: Margaret Thatcher
thatcher.bio: The "Iron Lady," she promoted privatization and free-market reforms and signed the Sino-British Joint Declaration.

gorbachev.name: Mikhail Gorbachev
gorbachev.bio: Pursued openness and reform, ended the Cold War, and oversaw the dissolution of the Soviet Union; won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1990.

claudiusptolemy.name: Ptolemy
claudiusptolemy.bio: Active in Alexandria in Roman times, his Almagest and its geocentric system dominated Western astronomy for 1,400 years. (Birth and death years are estimates.)

chenping.name: Chen Ping
chenping.bio: He first served Xiang Yu and then joined Liu Bang, devising many ingenious schemes; he drove Fan Zeng away with a ruse of sowing discord, and after Empress Lü's death helped Zhou Bo quell the Lü clan. (Birth year unknown.)

botticelli.name: Sandro Botticelli
botticelli.bio: Author of The Birth of Venus and Primavera, he was strongly patronized by the Medici and in later life followed Savonarola.

bramante.name: Donato Bramante
bramante.bio: A leading architect of the High Renaissance, he designed the new St. Peter's Basilica for Julius II.

shimazu.name: Shimazu Yoshihiro
shimazu.bio: A fierce commander of the Shimazu clan of Kyushu, he defeated the Ming army at Sacheon in the Imjin War and broke through the encirclement at Sekigahara to withdraw to Satsuma.

todo.name: Tōdō Takatora
todo.bio: A master castle builder who changed lords seven times in his life, he served successively the Azai, Toyotomi and Tokugawa, and was deeply trusted by Ieyasu.

wakisaka.name: Wakisaka Yasuharu
wakisaka.bio: One of the "Seven Spears of Shizugatake," he led the navy in the Imjin War and was routed by Yi Sun-sin at the Battle of Hansando.

meitner.name: Lise Meitner
meitner.bio: Working with Hahn, she researched nuclear fission; after going into exile in Sweden she was the first to explain the phenomenon physically.

goethe.name: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
goethe.bio: A giant of German literature, author of The Sorrows of Young Werther and Faust; he also studied color theory and plant morphology.
